label: Input/encoding phase from step 2 through <DEL>
explanation: Fires on almost every original-phase step from t=2 onward and on the <DEL> step (rate ~96-99% at orig_idx 2..8, 97% at <DEL>); essentially silent at t=0, t=1 (4.5%), and throughout the copy phase (0.2%). Token-identity independent (flat rates across in_tok, prev_tok, first_tok, n_digits). Within a sequence activation ramps up roughly monotonically over the original tokens and peaks at <DEL> (the <DEL> step alone carries ~21% of mass); top activations are short sequences (L=3-5) whose <DEL> step reaches ~0.9-1.0 of max, often with p/1 among the first tokens. Repeated tokens (in_first=0) still fire, so it is not a novelty detector. Lowest activations come from long sequences where early-step activations are small.

issues: Reproduced the test scores: P 0.975, R 0.990, F1 0.983, mass recall 0.9995, correlation 0.83.

Rate claims all check out on the test split. Firing rate is 0.0 at t=0, 0.045 at t=1, 0.973 at <DEL>, 0.002 in the copy phase, and 0.956-0.99 at orig_idx 2..8. The <DEL> step holds 21.4% of the activation mass.
Missed activations hold only 0.1% of the mass. They are tiny activations at t=1 and scattered small copy-phase activations at recall_idx 2-3, with no systematic pattern.

False positives are about 2.5% of predicted steps and spread out. They are a bit more common at t=2 (precision 0.956) and at <DEL> for L>=8 (precision 0.935), where activations at <DEL> fade in long sequences. These are small graded effects, not a separate class.
Token independence holds: repeated tokens (in_first==0) have precision 0.986, and precision for L=9 vs L<=4 is 0.978 vs 0.961.
Minor imprecision: 'from step 2' is accurate, but the magnitude claim 'rises steadily and peaks at <DEL>' was not checked per step. The mass shares are consistent with it.
